rv.q: It was a risk that there might be no new theatrical life in death but Eclipse has found it.
Touching, truthful writing and a gorgeous set elevate this familiar story of family bereavement
When salt of the earth carer, Karen (a marvellous Selina Cadell) asks anyone within earshot if they want a cup of tea, it's a straightforward enquiry about the desirability of a beverage.
This is probably the most completely perfect production we have seen in recent years.

‘ Eclipse ’ is a beautifully understated piece which resonates with something deeply human in us all, never needing to be anything more than it is to captivate the audience and take them on a journey of grief, struggle, care and hope.
Overall, Eclipse is a safe play that leans on well-worn stereotypes for its comedy, often at the expense of deeper emotional complexity.

cn.t: Critics praise John Morton's playwriting debut as a moving and reverent exploration of loss and family dynamics, with particular acclaim for its intimate staging at the Minerva Theatre and precisely crafted dialogue.
